subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should OpenClaw add a core ACP skill-context injection contract for `sessions_spawn`, and which selection modes plus redaction, observability, prompt-layer, and Codex-native interaction semantics are allowed?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but selecting explicit/default/auto behavior and deciding what local skill material may cross into ACP child harnesses changes a core session and security boundary that automation should not decide.

options.title: Design core ACP contract first
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers specify allowed selection modes, redaction/audit metadata, prompt layer, resume behavior, and harness-parity requirements before implementation.

options.title: Limit to agent-level skill filters
options.body: Do not add a per-spawn selector yet; rely on existing `agents.defaults.skills` and `agents.list[].skills` while the broader skill prompt contract is settled.

options.title: Decline core injection
options.body: Close this direction if maintainers decide ACP harnesses should not receive OpenClaw-rendered skills through `sessions_spawn`.

recommendation.title: Design core ACP contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers specify allowed selection modes, redaction/audit metadata, prompt layer, resume behavior, and harness-parity requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the central ACP sessions_spawn surface and have the strongest history signal for this product/security contract.
